planting.note: Set bulbs 2-3 inches deep in spring in well-drained garden soil in full sun, where warm-season rain events will trigger successive bloom flushes.

directions: Plant bulbs 2-3 inches deep in loose, well-drained soil in full sun; Prairie Sunset is a Zephyranthes hybrid selected for its warm coppery-peach to soft apricot-orange blooms, a color break from the more common pure pink, white, and yellow rain lily selections. Like other zephyr lilies, it stays dormant through dry spells and erupts into a synchronized flush of funnel-shaped flowers within a few days of a soaking rain or deep watering, repeating this cycle from late spring through early fall. Clumps bulk up steadily by offset division and are best left undisturbed for several years to build a dense, floriferous colony along walkways, rock gardens, or bed edges. Divide only when flowering noticeably declines from overcrowding.

subcategory: large-flowered South American rain lily bulb

planting.note: Plant bulbs 3-4 inches deep in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun where a summer downpour or deep irrigation will trigger a mass bloom flush within days.

directions: Set bulbs 3-4 inches deep in gritty, well-drained soil in full sun; 'Russell Manning' is a selected strain of the large-flowered Habranthus brachyandrus, chosen for exceptionally big, rosy-pink, maroon-throated blooms held at the tilted, 45-degree angle characteristic of the genus. It responds to a summer soaking the same way its parent species does, throwing up flower stalks and opening in near-unison within about a week of a heavy rain or thorough watering after a dry spell. Established clumps are long-lived and multiply gradually by bulb offsets, rewarding gardeners who leave them undisturbed in a sunny border or raised bed for years at a stretch. Because it tolerates only light, brief frost, gardeners north of zone 7 should grow it in containers or lift bulbs for winter storage.
